notes:
Summary: Veridian is a mid-market-to-enterprise customer-success SaaS that wants to add a fast, high-precision RAG layer to power a support assistant and ticket deflection. Primary drivers: reduce live-agent volume, raise top-5 answer precision for deflection, and keep per-query cost predictable.

Key requirements / ask: 
- Workload: hybrid of chat-driven assistant (agent assist + user self-help) and high-throughput knowledge search for ticket routing. Primary components: embedding index + neural reranker (2-stage retrieval).
- Indexing scale: plan to index ~6M canonical KB passages + ~1.2M historical tickets; after chunking expect ~9–12M vectors. Need estimates for memory/GPUs for Dedicated.
- Latency SLOs: end-to-end P95 target <= 350ms for deflection flow (retrieve + rerank + short LM answer). Retrieval-only P95 <= 120ms. Reranker slot must run within ~150–200ms.
- Quality targets: top-5 precision >= 88% on in-house labeled holdout; prefer reranking model configurable per route.
- Cost sensitivity: target blended cost per successful deflection query <= $0.04 (includes retrieval, rerank, and small LM concat for final output). Will trade slight latency increase for cost savings up to ~10% but NOT above SLO threshold.
- Model preferences: open to Redwood-verified dense embeddings (384–1536 dim) + GPU-optimized reranker; explicit interest in quantized CPU fallback for low-priority routes.
- Routing/fallbacks: must support policy-based routing by customer tier; automatic fallback to cheaper model variant if Dedicated capacity constrained.
- Security/compliance: VPC, SSO/SAML, strict retention controls, KMS integration, audit logs for all query traces; legal requires data residency in NA.

POC ask from Redwood: performance matrix for Dedicated instance sizes (mem/GPU), bench of 1M->10M vectors retrieval latency, benchmarked reranker P95 on 50k queries, cost-per-query simulation. Also need security packet (SOC2 + KMS integration notes) for procurement.

Quote from CTO (call 2024-11-05): "We need top-5 to actually help customers — if the first page is wrong, deflection hurts more than it helps. Latency has to feel instant to users. Can't trade the experience for a 3x cost increase."

Notes style: shorthand + bullet fragments common in SF deals. Priorities: 1) latency & precision, 2) cost predictability, 3) security/residency.
